claims.rationale: British retrospective own/allied and opponent counts. No artillery-personnel total tabulated or absent cavalry filled with zero; original Dutch/French returns uninspected.

claims.value: After reinforcements Siborne gives side A 15,750 infantry, 5,165 cavalry and 50 guns; side B successively 24,234 infantry/2,004 cavalry/40 guns, then 29,639/2,004/68. These are later cumulative populations, not opening strengths.
claims.rationale: Author-compiled successive field tables, no original timestamped returns authenticated. Artillery personnel excluded; no averaging with Bodart.

claims.value: Vaudoncourt’s side B table starts with Perponcher’s 8,000 infantry and 12 guns; by its five-o’clock stage it totals 44,200 infantry, 1,900 cavalry, 54 guns. This differs from Siborne’s later field totals and Bodart.
claims.rationale: Opponent estimate of changing coalition force, not British-only troops despite heading “Anglais”; no complete original national returns. English rendering (ours): "Perponcher: eight thousand infantry and twelve guns. At five o’clock, total forty-four thousand two hundred infantry, nineteen hundred cavalry and fifty-four guns."

claims.value: Ney held the French left-wing assignment, while Bachelu/Foy/Jérôme had local division roles. Orange/Perponcher covered the initial allied position; Wellington directed the reinforced army and Halkett/Kielmansegge received distinct brigade tasks.
claims.rationale: Successive superior, contingent and local scopes; no equal or continuous army-wide attribution. English rendering (ours): "Ney took command of the left wing; Bachelu advanced; Orange’s force comprised Perponcher’s division."
